posts.inspiredBy: Inspired by Vesalius's De Humani Corporis Fabrica anatomy engravings - created to turn the body into a couture specimen instead of a literal skeleton.
Inspired by Tutankhamun's gold death mask - created to make ancient regalia crack open into a live modern Devi reveal.
Inspired by Ingres's La Source and classical caryatid sculpture - created to make water remember the shape of a gown.
Inspired by broken Greek marble statues and the Hermes of Praxiteles - created to make museum damage feel alive, funny, and glamorous.
Inspired by Vermeer's Girl with a Pearl Earring - created to turn a single pearl into a whole celestial fashion moment.
Inspired by Leonardo da Vinci's Vitruvian Man - created to turn proportion, geometry, and anatomy into Devi's own living blueprint.
Inspired by Audubon's Birds of America - created to make embroidered plumage break free and become a living couture performance.
Inspired by Gustav Klimt's gilded portrait language in Adele Bloch-Bauer I - created to make ornament feel like anatomy under couture.
Inspired by Whistler's Mother - created to make stillness, shadow, and restraint feel uncanny and fully alive.
Inspired by NASA and Smithsonian X-ray imagery - created to make the dress feel like a living scan that reveals light instead of bone.
Inspired by Bosch's Garden of Earthly Delights - created to turn surreal garden life into Devi's own high-fashion parade.
Inspired by Picasso's Blue Period - created to let Devi step in and out of a painting without losing her glamour.
